Evaluating jihoo: Lessons for sci > Borrow Core, Drop Elaboration, Compile Speed

Borrow Core, Drop Elaboration, Compile Speed

Beyond proof-based check elimination, three more pieces of jihoo engineering transfer to sci — as techniques, not as semantics. SA's rules (&T permission decided by the Referee from the actual load or store, and SLA's ownership model above it) stay exactly as they are; what follows is about how the checking and lowering machinery is organized.

Borrow core: small kernel re-checks a big frontend

jihoo's check.jh (1,372 lines) does not trust its frontend: it recomputes all loans independently on MIR, so a frontend bug becomes a compile error instead of a dangling pointer. Three techniques are directly borrowable:

  • Loans as flat bit vectors per program point — joins and copies never allocate per local.
  • Function-level relations (parameter origin → returned view / inout store) derived by fixed point and maintained incrementally: when a relation grows, only direct callers are re-derived and only blocks whose loans changed are revisited; call sites use the derived relation instead of assuming the worst on every call.
  • LLVM attributes for borrowed parameters: noalias / dereferenceable / readonly, which the borrow rules guarantee. If sci does not annotate its borrowed parameters equivalently, this is a low-cost, direct-yield gap: the Referee already knows the facts, they are just not being handed to LLVM.

Not borrowable: jihoo's semantics (borrows never escape a function; borrow/inout/sink signatures make checking local). Moving them would redefine SA, not optimize sci.

Drop elaboration: insertion and pruning as separate passes

elab.jh (749 lines) tracks initialization on MIR in two deliberately separated steps: the semantic pass first inserts a drop for every owned local at scope exit, unconditionally; the elaborator then deletes drops for locals that were definitely moved, and generates a drop flag only for locals moved on some paths. Anything decidable statically never becomes a runtime flag — the Perceus-style division of labour.

sci/SLA's own recent defects live exactly on this surface: a select-case binding over-released by scope-exit retirement, and a struct-literal temporary double-freed by caller/callee drop disagreement. Both were static drop-placement decisions made in fused code. jihoo's organization — insertion and pruning as separate passes, pruning independently testable on MIR, plus a kill switch (JIHOO_NO_ELAB) to isolate the pass while diagnosing — is the structural fix worth copying. The ownership rules themselves remain SA's own.

Compile speed: where the 63 seconds actually go

  • Single-pass semantics: checking and lowering are fused; generics are processed per instantiation from a queue. The frontend never makes multiple AST passes — the structural reason it is only ~3% of a full build.
  • Text IR + dlopen libLLVM C API: no C++ shim, no headers; build and deployment stay light. (This one mainly informs the Rust sla backend's organization; sci's Zig route differs in shape.)
  • Codegen units: after optimization, a large module is split into at most 8 units, each with its own LLVM context, emitted in parallel (JIHOO_CODEGEN_UNITS). If sci emits large programs single-threaded, this is a ready-made speedup.

What does not transfer

  • Absolute compile times: jihoo's compiler is 53,489 lines with a smaller language surface; its 63-second bootstrap cannot be compared head-to-head with sci's. The transferable datum is the frontend's ~3% share.
  • Borrow semantics, as above: techniques yes, language definition no.
  • The proof engine's maturity caveat: jihoo's docs call the verification line research-grade from 0.6 on; the measured, shipping behaviour (default verify in every build, fixed-point bootstrap) is what this assessment relies on.

Sources: jihoo compiler/check.jh, elab.jh, backend.jh and internals docs at HEAD 5f18751…; measurements 2026-11-27 (see “jihoo Measure”). SLA-side defect references: select-case over-release and struct-literal double-free, both fixed in sa_plugin_sla (a8f635f8 / 19073ab4).
